A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 20-page versions of the same MELON research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; v4 adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v2 reports original AgentDojo experiments across three agent models, including defense comparisons, ablations, sensitivity tests, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original AgentDojo experiments, revises LLM-detector results, and adds detector accuracy and error-rate results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The masking procedure, task-neutral prompt, few-shot examples, tool-call cache, semantic comparison, and MELON-Aug combination are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the implementation descriptions match.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same AgentDojo domains and four attack types, together with the same preliminary VWA-Adv observation in Appendix D. Appendix F analyzes existing attack types without introducing new task or data coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Delimiting, Repeat Prompt, Tool Filter, DeBERTa Detector, and LLM Detector. TaskShield is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated. The LLM-detector description and prompt are unchanged despite revised scores.

E3.justification: Appendix F extends evaluation with detector accuracy, FPR, and FNR for three retained attack types, beyond the earlier end-to-end metrics and benign FPR analysis. Existing experimental settings are unchanged as documented; no protocol revision explains the replacement Table 1 results.

E4.justification: New Appendix F examines attack-specific LLM-detector errors despite zero reported attack success. The existing MELON component ablations, prompt and threshold sensitivity tests, false-positive examples, and attack-success analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix F adds classification performance estimates, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises a central baseline: LLM Detector average UA/ASR changes from 20.83%/1.27%, 14.11%/0.76%, and 17.61%/2.23% to 0%/0% for GPT-4o, o3-mini, and Llama-3.3-70B, respectively. Its BU for the latter two changes from 58.76% and 74.23% to 81.44%. Table 5 adds detector accuracy/FPR/FNR results. MELON and other comparator scores remain unchanged; these are reported replacements, not an established same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The formal state definitions, masking and similarity equations, ensemble detector, and Hoeffding-based error bounds in Section 3.4 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: detecting injection through reduced dependence on user input, with favorable security–utility performance and benefits from prompt augmentation. The title changes wording without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 revises the LLM-detector discussion from substantial false negatives to zero ASR and zero UA with small residual detection errors. Appendix F adds possible specialization to attack patterns as an explanation. MELON's existing applicability boundaries and failure interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. Existing prompts, tool-argument handling, embedding model, threshold, and computational-overhead information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add TaskShield by Jia et al. (2024), describing its tool-call alignment check against user tasks. The remaining related-work discussion and research positioning are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title and running headers, corrects the conference edition, edits parts of Section 4.2, and adds acknowledgements and Appendix F. The overall organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 5 and updates Figures 1 and 3, including axis adjustments accompanying the revised detector results. There are limited spacing and text-flow changes; existing table structures and method diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: The code link and detector diagnostics provide useful additions, but the substantial LLM-detector result replacements are unexplained. New Appendix F also reports 99.98% accuracy in prose, which matches none of Table 5's accuracy entries, while Section 4.4 retains its earlier characterization of poor LLM-detector detection capability. The PDFs do not establish whether the replacements correct earlier errors, and these unresolved consistency issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
